Q: How do binary, multiclass, multilabel and open-set classification differ?
explain: Binary classification chooses between two declared outcomes. Multiclass classification chooses one of several mutually exclusive labels. Multilabel classification permits several labels at once, often with one decision threshold per label. Open-set behavior adds a route for inputs outside the known taxonomy; it is not created automatically by using a softmax. Define whether a message can have both billing and access intent before selecting an algorithm. A forced single label can be wrong even if the model correctly notices both issues. Labels should have operational definitions, inclusion and exclusion examples, and an explicit ambiguity policy.
example: A message says a payment failed and the account is locked. A single-label router may ask which issue to handle first; a multilabel system may return billing and access. Neither should silently treat the second issue as irrelevant.
takeaway: Specify the label contract before optimizing a classifier.

Q: How do features, embeddings and generative LLM decisions fit into the same classification pipeline?
explain: A classical classifier consumes a representation such as numeric fields, token counts or TF-IDF weights. A neural embedding model instead encodes text into a dense vector; a nearest-prototype rule or supervised head can classify those vectors. A generative large language model can assign a label from instructions and examples without updating its weights. These are different stages and training choices, not interchangeable names for one algorithm. Compare them on the same frozen test set, including unknown and ambiguous inputs. Encoding a text does not by itself choose a label, and a generated label is not automatically supported or permitted.
example: One support message is represented as word features for logistic regression, as a sentence vector for a supervised head, and as input to a bounded label-producing prompt. All three must obey the same taxonomy and be checked against the same independent expected label.
takeaway: Keep representation, decision rule and output validation explicit.
